text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Cabinet orders monitoring of concerts to guarantee compliance with Islam's teachings, social norms. Islamist bid to ban concerts failed to win parliament's approval earlier in May.
- State-owned Kuwait Oil Company (KOC) and Saudi Arabian Texaco seek rise to 420,000 barrels per day in year 2005 at neutral zone between Kuwait and Saudi Arabia.
- Trade between Kuwait and Germany up by four percent to about $500 million in 1996.
- Austrian embassy official says Kuwait is an ideal market for investment.

- Parliament could discuss government bill that seeks authorisation to revive efforts to collect weapons kept by civilians. Large amounts of weapons were left by Iraqi troops as they fled during 1991 Gulf War that ended Baghdad's seven-month occupation.
- Kuwait's Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah to hold official talks with Sri Lanka's President Kumaratunga who arrived on Monday for three-day official visit.

- Government objects to parliamentary financial committee's suspension of budget bill. Panel has suspended proposed 1997/98 state budget over dispute about rise in income from charges on public services. State has accounted for proceeds of increase despite a ban on increasing state charges without parliament's approval.
- Arab Lawyers conference to discuss POW issue. Kuwait says Iraq still detains about 600 Kuwaitis since 1990-91 occupation; Iraq denies this.
